details:
NILAVE – Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a proposed visual decision-support concept designed to make lunar south pole landing-site planning easier to understand.

The concept focuses on two important mission-planning factors: sunlight availability for solar power generation and Earth visibility for direct-to-Earth communication. Users would select a candidate landing site and mission date/time, then compare the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local lunar horizon. Objects above the horizon may be visible, while objects below it may be obstructed by the local terrain.

The project aims to help mission planners compare different landing locations and dates more clearly. It can also support education and public understanding of the challenges involved in lunar exploration.

For future development, we identified NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO/LOLA) for lunar topography, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) for lunar imagery, and NASA/JPL Horizons for celestial position data. These are proposed data sources for integration.

Our creative approach is to bring two critical mission questions—solar power potential and communication visibility—into one simple visual comparison concept. We considered terrain elevation, local horizon obstruction, sunlight, Earth visibility, mission date/time, and ease of use.

Tools and technologies: The current submission was prepared as a PowerPoint-based concept presentation and interface mock-up. No programming language, hardware, live calculations, or real-time data integration has been used in this submission. These are planned for future development.

Intended impact: NILAVE aims to make complex lunar visibility information easier to interpret and support more informed comparisons of potential lunar landing sites. Working calculations, NASA data integration, and an interactive web application are planned next steps.
